content.content:
1	# DEVDESK-505 (NX-02) — le banc contient des images connues et un amont qu'on peut couper
2	
3	Base : `main` à `75ec254e` (NX-01 mergé, #420). Story : `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`,
4	section NX-02 (7 critères, notés CA1 à CA7) et son « Report de NX-01 » (créer le proxy, l'ajouter
5	au groupe, commiter le nouveau `descriptor.json`). Plan écrit par l'architect ; rien n'est
6	implémenté. Aucune action sur le cluster pour ce plan : lecture du code, de
7	`docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`, de `skopeo --version` sur l'hôte (1.18.0 ; `crane`, `regctl`,
8	`oras` absents) et une recherche web sur le routage par chemin de Nexus.
9	
10	## Questions bloquantes
11	
12	Q1 à Q4 changent la conception des étapes 3, 4, 5 et 7 ; elles doivent être tranchées avant ces
13	étapes. Les étapes 1, 2 (sauf le Service de l'amont) et 6 peuvent partir sans elles. Q5 change le
14	découpage dans Plane.
15	
16	**Q1. Client sans démon pour pousser et tirer.**
17	- (a) **`skopeo` de l'hôte** (recommandé) : présent (1.18.0), client de référence indépendant du
18	  code de DevDesk (on ne mesure pas Nexus avec le code qui l'a peuplé), gère seul l'aller-retour
19	  HTTPS→HTTP, le défi Basic/Bearer de Nexus et `--preserve-digests`. Coût : un binaire non géré par
20	  mise (version de l'hôte, non épinglée), un second fichier qui lance un processus (`skopeo.go`,
21	  garde de source à élargir), une erreur `SkopeoMissing` claire.
22	- (b) `crane` installé par mise (aqua `google/go-containerregistry`), déclaré sur les tâches comme
23	  `kubectl` : version épinglée et reproductible ; contredit le « présent sur l'hôte » de la story
24	  (un outil de plus à installer).
25	- (c) Client Go natif (API OCI Distribution en `net/http`) : aucun outil, tout testable en
26	  `httptest` ; mais il faut réécrire push, pull et le jeton Bearer de Nexus (environ 400 lignes) et
27	  ce client partagerait les biais de celui qu'on mesure dans NX-03 à NX-05.
28	
29	**Q2. Source des images de départ.**
30	- (a) **Images générées en Go au moment du peuplement** (recommandé) : un OCI layout écrit dans un
31	  dossier temporaire par un générateur déterministe (couche tar non compressée, pas d'horodatage,
32	  config sans `created`) ; digests stables et connus d'avance (épinglés dans un golden), aucun
33	  binaire versionné, aucun réseau, quelques Ko par image. Risque : Nexus refuse une couche non
34	  compressée (H-LAYER, repli : gzip, digests alors liés à la version de Go).
35	- (b) OCI layout committé sous `testdata/` : même déterminisme, mais des blobs opaques dans le dépôt
36	  et un outil pour les régénérer.
37	- (c) Petite image publique (busybox) copiée de Docker Hub : dépend du réseau et des quotas, index
38	  multi-architecture, tag mutable (épinglage par digest obligatoire), plusieurs Mo.
39	
40	**Q3. Persistance de l'amont pendant la coupure (CA4 « avec le contenu d'avant la coupure »).**
41	- (a) **PVC `bench-upstream-data`** (`local-path`, 1Gi, `ReadWriteOnce`, `Recreate`)
42	  (recommandé) : le contenu survit au passage à 0 réplica, `restore` ne fait que remonter à 1 et
43	  attendre ; détruit avec le namespace. Coût : la remise à zéro de l'amont supprime et recrée ce PVC
44	  (droit `delete persistentvolumeclaims` dans le namespace).
45	- (b) `emptyDir` + repeuplement par `restore` : plus simple côté Kubernetes, mais `restore` exige
46	  skopeo et le port-forward, est plus lent, et tout contenu ajouté à la main dans l'amont (NX-04)
47	  est perdu à la coupure.
48	
49	**Q4. Comment la machine de dev atteint l'amont pour le peupler.** L'amont n'a pas
50	d'authentification (le proxy le lit sans identifiant).
51	- (a) **`kubectl port-forward` le temps du peuplement** (recommandé) : l'amont reste interne au
52	  cluster (ClusterIP seul), rien n'est inscriptible depuis le LAN, aucun NodePort consommé, aucun
53	  secret de plus. Coût : un processus long dans `kubectl.go` (démarrage, lecture de la ligne
54	  `Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:<port>`, arrêt), droit `create pods/portforward`.
55	- (b) NodePort 30483 (bloc réservé) sans authentification : le plus simple ; mais un registre
56	  **inscriptible par tout le LAN** tant que le banc existe (risque à accepter explicitement, plus
57	  grave que la lecture anonyme de Nexus déjà acceptée).
58	- (c) NodePort 30483 + htpasswd : un Secret dans le namespace, des identifiants pour le proxy Nexus
59	  (`httpClient.authentication`) et dans le fichier de secrets ; plus de code et plus de surface.
60	
61	**Q5. Effort et découpage.** L'effort annoncé (M) est **sous-estimé : L** (voir « Effort »).
62	- (a) **Découper** (recommandé) : NX-02a « amont, proxy créé, peuplement, descripteur » (CA1, CA2,
63	  CA3, CA5, CA6 ; M) puis NX-02b « couper/rétablir l'amont, remise à zéro » (CA4, CA7 ; M). NX-03
64	  ne dépend que de NX-02a ; NX-04 dépend des deux.
65	- (b) Garder une story L.
66	
67	## Faits qui complètent la story
68	
69	| # | Fait | Effet sur le plan |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| F1 | `UpstreamURL` vaut déjà `http://bench-upstream.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:5000` (`params.go:148`) | nom du Service `bench-upstream`, port 5000 : imposés |
72	| F2 | Le proxy est créé sans `pathEnabled` ni connecteur ; seul le groupe a `docker.httpPort` 8082 (`provision.go`, `repositories()`) | pousser vers `docker-hosted` et tirer par `docker-proxy` passe par le **routage par chemin** sur 8081 (H-PATH) |
73	| F3 | Nexus 3.98.1 refuse un proxy dont l'hôte amont ne résout pas ; le DNS d'un Service existe dès sa création, pod prêt ou non | il suffit que le Service existe avant `Provision` ; on attend quand même l'amont prêt (peuplement) |
74	| F4 | Le proxy est créé avec `negativeCache` 1440 min et `httpClient.autoBlock: true` | après un rétablissement, le proxy peut rester bloqué ou garder des 404 en cache : `restore` doit le débloquer (H-UNBLOCK) |
75	| F5 | `kubectl apply --server-side` revendique les champs qu'il écrit ; `kubectl scale` en prend un autre gestionnaire | le Deployment de l'amont **n'écrit pas `replicas`** (sinon conflit SSA ou un `up` qui rétablit en douce) |
76	| F6 | `Deploy` ne lit que les pods `app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus` (`deploy.go:20`) | l'attente et le diagnostic sont paramétrés par sélecteur pour servir aussi l'amont |
77	| F7 | Garde `execAllowed = {kubectl.go, secrets.go}` (`guard_test.go:413`) | `skopeo.go` s'y ajoute (option Q1 a) |
78	| F8 | Recherche web : le routage par chemin Docker existe depuis 3.83 (image `hôte:8081/<dépôt>/<nom>`) ; « par défaut » n'est pas confirmé par Sonatype | H-PATH vérifiée à l'étape 0, avant le code |
79	| F9 | Toute requête d'une image non en cache **à travers le proxy ou le groupe** la met en cache | les tests et NX-03 à NX-05 ne lisent `mirror/uncached` que par l'API REST des composants ; sinon `reset` |
80	
81	## Exigences non fonctionnelles
82	
83	- **Charge** : l'amont demande 50m/64Mi (limites 500m/256Mi), un PVC de 1Gi (non appliqué par
84	  `local-path`) ; le jeu de données pèse quelques Ko. Le nœud est engagé à environ 84 % en limites :
85	  l'amont reste négligeable.
86	- **Durée** : `seed` < 1 min ; `cut` < 30 s (fin du pod) ; `restore` < 1 min ; `reset` < 2 min ;
87	  le délai d'échec du proxy amont coupé est **mesuré** à l'étape 11 (H-CUTDELAY), il conditionne
88	  NX-04.
89	- **Sécurité** : TLS désactivé seulement pour des références dont l'hôte est `127.0.0.1` (Nexus) ou
90	  l'adresse du port-forward (loopback) ; aucun identifiant en argument de processus (fichier
91	  d'authentification temporaire `0600` dans un dossier `0700`, supprimé à la fin) ; environnement
92	  de skopeo nettoyé (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, `REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE`, `CONTAINERS_*` ; `registries.conf` vide
93	  et politique explicite) ; ni stderr de skopeo ni de kubectl dans un message ; aucun mot de passe
94	  dans le descripteur ni dans une sortie (`requireQuiet` étendu).
95	- **Exploitabilité** : chaque erreur reste un `*BenchError` (cause + vérification) ; `status` dit
96	  l'état de l'amont (prêt, coupé, absent) et du jeu de données (conforme, différent).
97	- **Hors cluster** : rien de ceci ne tourne dans `mise run ci` ni en CI ; tests d'intégration gardés.
98	
99	## Décisions (sous réserve de Q1 à Q4 ; options recommandées retenues)
100	
101	- **D-G** Amont : Deployment `bench-upstream` (image `docker.io/library/registry:3.0.0`, épinglée,
102	  paramétrable par `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE` / `_UPSTREAM_IMAGE_TAG`, refus du préfixe
103	  `tvp-zot.incus:5000` par le même `validateImage`), PVC `bench-upstream-data`, Service ClusterIP
104	  `bench-upstream:5000`. Sans `replicas` (F5), `Recreate`, UID/GID 1000, `runAsNonRoot`, `drop:
105	  [ALL]`, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`, pas de jeton de compte de service, `readinessProbe` `GET /v2/`
106	  sur 5000, env `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none` (distribution v3 trace par défaut). Mêmes labels
107	  `managed-by` / `part-of`, `app.kubernetes.io/name: bench-upstream`.
108	- **D-H** Peuplement par skopeo (Q1 a), depuis un OCI layout généré en Go (Q2 a), poussé vers
109	  l'amont par port-forward (Q4 a), vers `docker-hosted` par chemin sur `127.0.0.1:<HTTPNodePort>`
110	  avec le compte admin, tiré à travers `docker-proxy` par chemin avec `bench-pull` (toujours ce
111	  compte, qui marche que l'accès anonyme soit actif ou non).
112	  `--preserve-digests` partout : un digest qui changerait fait échouer le peuplement.
113	- **D-I** Jeu de données fixe, dans le code (`dataset.go`), et décrit dans le descripteur :
114	
115	  | Image | Où | Rôle (scénario) |
116	  |---|---|---|
117	  | `api:1.0.0`, `api:1.1.0` | `docker-hosted` | hosted ; nom à un composant, deux tags |
118	  | `team/api:1.0.0` | `docker-hosted` | nom à deux composants |
119	  | `tools/cli:0.1.0` | `docker-hosted` | troisième image du hosted |
120	  | `shared/base:1.0` | `docker-hosted` **et** amont | doublon dans le groupe (contenus différents, digests différents) |
121	  | `mirror/cached:1.0` | amont, tirée par le proxy | « proxy rempli », seulement dans le proxy |
122	  | `mirror/uncached:1.0` | amont, jamais tirée | « proxy vide » pour ce nom, « partiellement en cache » |
123	
124	  Chaque image porte un fichier `/bench/<source>/<nom>-<tag>.txt` et un label
125	  `org.devdesk.nexus-bench.source` (`hosted` ou `upstream`), d'où des digests distincts.
126	  Hypothèse : le doublon a deux contenus différents (une lecture par le groupe dit quel membre a
127	  répondu) ; s'il doit être identique, une ligne de la table change.
128	- **D-J** `up` = déployer (Nexus + amont) → amont à 1 réplica et prêt → provisionner (le proxy est
129	  maintenant créé et membre du groupe) → peupler → descripteur. Le descripteur reste écrit
130	  seulement après un succès complet. Hypothèse : `up` rétablit un amont coupé (il ramène le banc à
131	  son état nominal) et le dit sur sa sortie.
132	- **D-K** Couper/rétablir : `cut-upstream` = `kubectl scale deployment/bench-upstream
133	  --replicas=0` puis attente de la disparition du pod ; `restore-upstream` = `--replicas=1`, attente
134	  du pod prêt, puis déblocage du proxy par REST (`PUT` de sa configuration inchangée, qui remet son
135	  client HTTP à neuf, puis `POST /v1/repositories/docker-proxy/invalidate-cache`, qui vide le cache
136	  négatif), puis vérification que les manifestes de l'amont ont les digests du jeu de données.
137	  Hypothèse prudente : les réglages du proxy (`autoBlock`, délais du client HTTP) restent ceux de
138	  NX-01 et de Nexus, pour que NX-04 mesure le comportement par défaut ; à revoir si H-CUTDELAY
139	  dépasse 60 s.
140	- **D-L** Remise à zéro (`reset`) sans toucher l'instance : `DELETE` de `docker-group`,
141	  `docker-proxy`, `docker-hosted` (dans cet ordre, 404 accepté), remise à neuf du stockage de
142	  l'amont (0 réplica, suppression du PVC `bench-upstream-data`, `apply` du flux complet, 1 réplica,
143	  prêt), puis `Provision` (recrée les trois dépôts, idempotent) et `Seed`. Jamais : le namespace, le
144	  Deployment `nexus`, son pod, le PVC `nexus-data`. Rejeté : supprimer les composants un par un
145	  (`DELETE /v1/components/{id}`), qui laisse des couches orphelines visibles dans les mesures.
146	- **D-M** Descripteur en **schéma 2** : `LoadDescriptor` n'accepte plus que 2 (un fichier v1 dit
147	  « run mise run nexus-bench:up »). Ajouts, dans cet ordre après `accounts` : `registryAccess`
148	  (`scheme: "http"`, `tlsVerify: false`, `routing: "path"`), `upstream` (`service`, `image`,
149	  `url`, `persistent: true`, `exposure: "port-forward"`), `dataset` (liste ordonnée de
150	  `{name, tag, digest, location, cachedInProxy}`). Aucun secret, aucun horodatage.
151	
152	## Composants et flux
153	
154	```
155	up:      Preflight(OpUp) → apply ns → apply flux (nexus + amont) → wait nexus (Deploy)
156	         → EnsureUpstream (scale 1, wait ready) → Provision (proxy créé) → Seed → descriptor v2
157	seed:    Preflight(OpSeed) → upstream prêt ? → Seed → descriptor v2
158	Seed:    BuildLayout(tmp) → PortForward(svc/bench-upstream:5000) → copy amont (skopeo)
159	         → stop forward → copy hosted (skopeo, admin, 127.0.0.1:HTTPNodePort/docker-hosted/…)
160	         → pull-through (skopeo, bench-pull, …/docker-proxy/…, vers dir temporaire)
161	         → vérifie par REST les composants de docker-proxy = ensemble attendu
162	cut:     Preflight(OpCut) → scale 0 → wait no pod
163	restore: Preflight(OpRestore) → scale 1 → wait ready → unblock proxy (REST) → verify digests amont
164	reset:   Preflight(OpReset) → delete repos (REST) → recycle upstream storage → Provision → Seed
165	status:  + ligne `upstream:` (ready / cut / missing) + ligne `dataset:` (matches / differs / unknown)
166	```
167	
168	Nouveaux fichiers (tous dans `internal/nexusbench`) : `manifests/40-upstream-pvc.yaml.tmpl`,
169	`50-upstream-deployment.yaml.tmpl`, `60-upstream-service.yaml.tmpl`, `dataset.go`,
170	`ocilayout.go`, `skopeo.go`, `upstream.go`, `seed.go`, `reset.go`. Le port-forward vit dans
171	`kubectl.go` (une seule porte vers le cluster), pas dans un fichier à lui. Modifiés : `params.go`,
172	`render.go`, `deploy.go`, `preflight.go`, `errors.go`, `nexusapi.go`, `provision.go`,
173	`descriptor.go`, `descriptor.json`, `testdata/*`, `guard_test.go`, `mise_tasks_test.go`,
174	`fakenexus_test.go`, `cmd/nexus-bench/*`, `mise.toml`, `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.
175	
176	## Étapes
177	
178	Chaque étape : tests écrits d'abord par le `tester`, puis le code ; `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`
179	mis à jour dans le même commit ; `go test ./internal/nexusbench/...` vert ; `mise run lint` vert.
180	Code, commentaires, sorties et erreurs en anglais US. Commande ciblée par défaut :
181	`go test -count=1 ./internal/nexusbench/... -run '<motif>'`.
182	
183	### Étape 0 — Lever H-PATH et H-PUSH sur le banc actuel (½ jour, manuel, exige l'accord d'agir sur `datomir`)
184	
185	Pas de code commité. Sur le banc NX-01 en place : lire `/service/rest/swagger.json` (champ de
186	routage par chemin des dépôts Docker et sa valeur par défaut) ; `GET` des dépôts `docker-hosted`
187	(champ de routage tel que créé) ; pousser **une** image de test avec
188	`skopeo copy --dest-tls-verify=false --dest-authfile <tmp> oci:<layout>:img
189	docker://127.0.0.1:30481/docker-hosted/probe:1` (layout fait à la main), avec une couche non
190	compressée (H-LAYER) ; la relire. Elle sera effacée par le premier `reset` (ou par `down`).
191	**Critère de fin** : H-PATH, H-PUSH, H-LAYER notées vraies ou fausses dans la section « Hypothèses »
192	de `nexus-bench.md`. Si H-PATH est fausse : ajouter le champ de routage au payload des dépôts
193	hosted et proxy à l'étape 6 ; si le routage par chemin n'existe pas sur 3.98.1, revenir vers
194	l'utilisateur (connecteurs par port pour hosted et proxy, qui empiètent sur NX-05).
195	
196	### Étape 1 — Paramètres de l'amont (parallélisable avec 3 et 4)
197	
198	- `params.go` : champs `UpstreamImage`, `UpstreamImageTag` ; variables
199	  `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE` (défaut `docker.io/library/registry`) et
200	  `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE_TAG` (défaut `3.0.0`) ; `func (p Params) UpstreamImageRef() string` ;
201	  `func (p Params) UpstreamIsBench() bool` (vrai quand `UpstreamURL == upstreamFor(Namespace)`).
202	- `Validate` : `validateImage` réutilisé avec les noms de variables de l'amont (refactor :
203	  `validateImage(envImage, envTag, image, tag)`).
204	- Tests (`params_test.go`, table) : défauts ; variable vide = non posée ; `tvp-zot.incus:5000/x` →
205	  erreur qui nomme `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE` ; tag invalide → erreur nommant
206	  `_UPSTREAM_IMAGE_TAG` ; `UpstreamIsBench` faux pour une URL personnalisée, vrai après
207	  `NEXUS_BENCH_NAMESPACE=x` seul.
208	- `cmd/nexus-bench/flags.go` : `--upstream-image`, `--upstream-image-tag` ; `describesDefaultBench`
209	  les couvre déjà (DeepEqual). Test : drapeau > variable > défaut.
210	- **Fin** : `go test ./internal/nexusbench/... -run 'Params|Env|Validate|Flag'` vert.
211	
212	### Étape 2 — Manifestes de l'amont (dépend de 1)
213	
214	- `manifests/40-upstream-pvc.yaml.tmpl` (PVC `bench-upstream-data`, 1Gi, RWO, sans classe),
215	  `50-upstream-deployment.yaml.tmpl` (D-G, **sans `replicas`**), `60-upstream-service.yaml.tmpl`
216	  (ClusterIP, port `registry` 5000 → 5000). `manifestTemplates` les ajoute après le Service
217	  `nexus` ; `manifestData.UpstreamImage`.
218	- Tests (`render_test.go`) : golden régénéré (`-update`, diff relu) ; l'ordre des sept documents ;
219	  `replicas` absent du Deployment `bench-upstream` (et présent, 1, dans `nexus`) ; aucun
220	  `nodePort` ni `type: NodePort` sur `bench-upstream` ; labels `managed-by`/`part-of` sur chaque
221	  objet ; image citée (`q`) ; `tvp-zot.incus:5000` dans l'image de l'amont → pas d'octets, erreur
222	  de Validate ; `TestRenderIgnoresParamsTheManifestsDoNotCarry` étendu (l'URL de l'amont ne change
223	  toujours rien) ; toujours ni Secret ni mot `password`/`secret`.
224	- **Fin** : `-run Render` vert ; `mise run nexus-bench:render` montre les sept documents.
225	
226	### Étape 3 — Jeu de données et OCI layout déterministe (parallélisable avec 1, 2, 4)
227	
228	- `dataset.go` :
229	  ```go
230	  type Location string // "docker-hosted" or "upstream"
231	  type DatasetImage struct {
232	      Name, Tag     string
233	      Location      Location
234	      PullThrough   bool   // pulled once through docker-proxy by Seed
235	      Digest        string // manifest digest, sha256:...
236	  }
237	  func Dataset() []DatasetImage // fixed order of D-I, digests filled from the generator
238	  ```
239	- `ocilayout.go` :
240	  ```go
241	  // WriteLayout writes an OCI image layout holding every image of images under dir
242	  // (which must exist and be empty) and returns the reference name of each image in
243	  // the layout, in the same order. The bytes depend on the images alone.
244	  func WriteLayout(dir string, images []DatasetImage) (refs []string, err error)
245	  func imageDigest(img DatasetImage) string // computed without writing anything
246	  ```
247	  Couche tar non compressée (`application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar`), entrées triées, `ModTime`
248	  zéro, uid/gid 0, mode fixe ; config OCI `linux/amd64` sans `created`, `rootfs.diff_ids` ;
249	  manifeste OCI v1 ; `index.json` avec `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name` = `img-NN` (le `:` du
250	  tag gênerait la syntaxe `oci:<dir>:<ref>` de skopeo) ; fichier `oci-layout`. Repli H-LAYER : une
251	  constante bascule en gzip (`gzip.Writer` sans nom ni date).
252	- Tests : deux appels donnent les mêmes octets et digests ; golden des digests
253	  (`testdata/dataset-digests.golden`) ; les deux `shared/base:1.0` ont des digests différents ;
254	  `index.json` valide (chaque blob référencé existe et son sha256 correspond) ; dossier non vide →

1053	## First real run (datomir, 2026-11-16)
1054	
1055	Step 10, on k0s v1.36 (`datomir`), image `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:3.98.1`
1056	(pulled in 10.6 s), `Server: Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)`. The operator accepted
1057	the Community EULA before the run; the REST client never accepts it on its own.
1058	
1059	**Deployment (H-RES).** First `up` on an empty cluster namespace: 48 s from the
1060	apply to a Ready pod and a changed admin password (pull included); the pod went
1061	Pending, ContainerCreating, running not ready, ready, and the claim bound with
1062	the pod (`local-path`). Idle after provisioning: 55m CPU and 1257Mi memory
1063	(`kubectl top pod`), against the 3Gi request and 4Gi limit of D-C: the request
1064	could be lowered, but it was kept (the JVM grows with the first pulls, to be

1066	the password is changed through the API (H-REST confirmed). An `up` on an
1067	already provisioned namespace takes 1 to 2 s.
1068	
1069	**REST statuses seen** (Nexus `request.log`): `PUT .../users/admin/change-password`
1070	204, `POST /system/eula` 204, `PUT /security/realms/active` 204, `PUT
1071	/security/anonymous` 200, `POST /security/roles` 200, `POST /security/users`
1072	200, `POST /repositories/docker/hosted` 201, `POST .../group` 201, `PUT
1073	/security/roles/{id}` 204, `PUT /security/users/{id}` 204, `PUT
1074	.../users/{id}/change-password` 204, `PUT .../hosted/{name}` and `PUT
1075	.../group/{name}` 204. The swagger lists the same codes (`GET /v1/system/eula`
1076	answers 200 whatever the state, `POST` 204/500). The client accepts any 2xx; the
1077	fake answers 200 for `POST` roles and users and 201 for repositories, as the
1078	swagger and the instance do.
1079	
1080	**The proxy.** `POST /repositories/docker/proxy` with
1081	`http://bench-upstream.nexus-bench.svc.cluster.local:5000`, a host that does not
1082	exist yet (NX-02): `400`, content type `application/vnd.siesta-validation-errors-v1+json`,
1083	body `[{"id":"HelperBean.proxy.remoteUrl","message":"Proxy URL blocked: Failed to
1084	resolve host: ..."}]`. The proxy is not created, the instance keeps working. The
1085	answer to this is in "REST client and provisioning", step 9: the proxy is
1086	pending, the group holds `docker-hosted` alone, the descriptor says so. The
1087	committed `descriptor.json` therefore describes the bench as it is before NX-02:
1088	`docker-hosted` and `docker-group` (with `docker-hosted` as its only member), no
1089	proxy. It is not the descriptor of the bench after NX-02, which has the proxy and
1090	lists it in the group, so the versioned file differs before and after NX-02. It
1091	also embeds the node IP `192.168.1.31`, which is specific to this machine.
1092	
1093	**CA2 (REST provisioning) is met for `docker-hosted` and `docker-group`; the
1094	proxy is deferred to NX-02.** Nexus 3.98.1-01 refuses a proxy whose upstream host
1095	does not resolve, and the upstream only exists once NX-02 deploys it. The
1096	criterion to carry into NX-02: run `mise run nexus-bench:up` again, check that
1097	`docker-proxy` exists and is a member of `docker-group`, and commit the new
1098	`descriptor.json`.
1099	
1100	**Idempotence (CA3).** A second and third `up` sent no `POST` but the refused
1101	proxy one (the pending proxy of "The proxy" above), `PUT` everything else (including a `change-password` of `bench-pull`
1102	with the stored password, the same value), left every password unchanged and
1103	wrote byte for byte the same `descriptor.json`. The lifecycle test compares the
1104	snapshots of repositories, roles and users after a second up and provision and
1105	finds them equal.
1106	
1107	**Read-only tests.** `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed`,
1108	`TestIntegrationAnonymousAsDescribed` and `TestIntegrationPullAccountIsReadOnly`
1109	pass: status 200 without credentials, the anonymous settings and the anonymous
1110	`GET /repositories` as described, and the control `POST` of `bench-pull` is
1111	refused with 403 (nothing was created).
1112	
1113	**Lifecycle (CA3, CA4).** `TestIntegrationLifecycle` passes in 151 s: up,
1114	provision, up and provision again with no change, `down`, `up` on a fresh
1115	instance (a new pod with a new `admin.password`), `down`. Afterwards the namespace
1116	is `NotFound`, no PersistentVolume of the bench remains (`local-path` reclaims
1117	with `Delete`), `secrets.json` is removed (the empty `datomir` folder above it
1118	stays) and `descriptor.json` is unchanged.
1119	
1120	## Data set and OCI layout (`dataset.go`, `ocilayout.go`, DEVDESK-538)
1121	
1122	The images the bench holds are fixed in code (decision D-I of DEVDESK-505), in
1123	this order. `Dataset()` returns a copy of the table with `Digest` filled by the
1124	generator; the digests are never written by hand.
1125	
1126	| Image | `Location` | Role |
1127	|---|---|---|
1128	| `api:1.0.0`, `api:1.1.0` | `docker-hosted` | one-component name, two tags |
1129	| `team/api:1.0.0` | `docker-hosted` | two-component name |
1130	| `tools/cli:0.1.0` | `docker-hosted` | third hosted image |
1131	| `shared/base:1.0` | `docker-hosted` and `upstream` | same name and tag in both places, different contents and digests, so a read through the group says which member answered |
1132	| `mirror/cached:1.0` | `upstream`, `PullThrough` | pulled once through `docker-proxy`, so only in the proxy |
1133	| `mirror/uncached:1.0` | `upstream` | never pulled |
1134	
1135	`WriteLayout(dir, images)` writes an OCI image layout into an existing, empty
1136	directory (anything else is an error and nothing is written: the images are built in
1137	memory first) and returns the reference of each image, `img-01`, `img-02`, ...
1138	(a `:` would break skopeo's `oci:<dir>:<ref>` syntax). `imageDigest(img)` gives the
1139	manifest digest without writing. The bytes depend on `Name`, `Tag` and `Location`
1140	only (not on `Digest` or `PullThrough`), with the standard library alone:
1141	
1142	- one layer per image, an uncompressed tar (`application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar`),
1143	  entries in sorted order (`bench/`, `bench/<source>/`, `bench/<source>/<name>-<tag>.txt`,
1144	  `/` of the name replaced by `-`), USTAR, `ModTime` at the Unix epoch, uid/gid 0,
1145	  no owner names, modes 0755 (folders) and 0644 (file);
1146	- config `linux/amd64`, no `created`, label `org.devdesk.nexus-bench.source`
1147	  (`hosted` or `upstream`) under the key `config.Labels`, spelled as the image spec
1148	  does (`TestWriteLayoutConfigKeyIsLabelsAsTheImageSpecSpellsIt`), `rootfs.diff_ids` holding the layer digest;
1149	- OCI v1 manifest, `index.json` with `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name`, and the
1150	  `oci-layout` file (`1.0.0`); JSON written by `encoding/json` from structs, so the
1151	  key order is fixed.
1152	
1153	`testdata/dataset-digests.golden` holds one line per image
1154	(`name:tag<TAB>location<TAB>digest`), rewritten with
1155	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestDatasetDigestsGolden -update`; a change of
1156	the generator moves every digest and shows in its diff.
1157	
1158	**H-LAYER fallback.** The constant `layerGzip` (`ocilayout.go`) is `false`. Setting
1159	it to `true` writes the layer with `compress/gzip` (no name, no date,
1160	`application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip`); the diff id stays the digest of the
1161	tar. The tests that pin the uncompressed layer (`TestWriteLayoutLayerIsAn...`,
1162	`TestWriteLayoutConfig`) and the golden then have to follow, and the digests depend on
1163	the `compress/gzip` output of the Go version.
1164	
1165	**Confirmed on the bench.** Nexus 3.98.1 accepts the uncompressed layer under
1166	`strictContentTypeValidation` (H-LAYER), skopeo with `--preserve-digests` pushes the
1167	layout to the upstream and to `docker-hosted` without changing a digest (H-PUSH), and
1168	`docker-proxy` keeps the upstream digest of `mirror/cached:1.0` on pull-through
1169	("Observed on the real bench (NX-02a)").
1170	
1171	## The two process doors: port-forward and skopeo (`kubectl.go`, `skopeo.go`, DEVDESK-539)
1172	
1173	NX-02 needs two more processes: a `kubectl port-forward` to reach the upstream
1174	registry Service from this machine, and `skopeo` to push the data set into it and
1175	into the bench Nexus. Both are started from one file each, and both are written so
1176	that a failure leaves no process and no secret behind.
1177	
1178	**Port-forward.** `PortForwarder.Forward(ctx, namespace, service, port)` runs
1179	`kubectl --context <c> -n <ns> port-forward svc/<service> :<port> --address
1180	127.0.0.1` (`NewExecPortForwarder`, `KubectlMissing` like `NewExecRunner`; the
1181	namespace and the Service name are checked against a DNS-like pattern first) and
1182	returns `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the port kubectl chose, with a `stop` function.
1183	
1184	- The address comes from `parseForwardingLine`, which accepts only
1185	  `Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:<port> -> ...` with a port from 1 to 65535; the IPv6
1186	  line kubectl prints as well, another address, and `127.0.0.1.evil.com` are
1187	  ignored. The wait is `portForwardTimeout` (15 s, a variable so a test can shorten
1188	  it); a `Deadline` `BenchError` after it.
1189	- One goroutine calls `cmd.Wait`, so kubectl is always reaped, whoever ended it.
1190	  `stop` kills the process and waits for that goroutine, any number of times
1191	  (`sync.Once`), and always returns nil. The cancellation of `ctx` kills kubectl
1192	  too (`exec.CommandContext`), whether `Forward` is still waiting (it kills, waits
1193	  and returns an error) or has returned. After every error path the process is
1194	  gone.
1195	- kubectl exiting before the line is a `BenchError` whose kind comes from
1196	  `classifyKubectl(stderr)`; the stderr (capped at 16 KiB) picks the kind and is
1197	  never put in a message.
1198	
1199	**skopeo.** `ImageCopier` has two methods, `Copy(ctx, src, dst, CopyOptions)` and
1200	`ManifestDigest(ctx, ref, creds)`; `ImageRef{Transport, Location}` is `oci`, `dir` or
1201	`docker` (the location of a docker reference has no `//`). `NewSkopeoCopier` finds
1202	skopeo on PATH (`SkopeoMissing`).
1203	
1204	- *Loopback only.* TLS verification is switched off (`--src-tls-verify=false`,
1205	  `--dest-tls-verify=false`, `--tls-verify=false`) for every docker reference and
1206	  for no other, so the host is the only protection: `checkSide` refuses, **before
1207	  anything is created or started**, a docker reference whose host is not one of
1208	  the two literals `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` (an optional port), or that has no `/`
1209	  followed by a repository name: without one skopeo reads `localhost:5000` as an
1210	  image of docker.io, with TLS off. `localhost` is not accepted, it resolves
1211	  through the host's configuration. The host is the text before the first `/`,
1212	  parsed with `net.SplitHostPort` (never a prefix test), so `127.0.0.1@evil.com`,
1213	  `127.0.0.1.evil.com`, `127.0.0.1:5000@evil.com`, `localhost`, `localhost.evil.com`
1214	  and `evil.com/127.0.0.1:5000/x` are refused, as are a LAN address (the node
1215	  itself), an empty host and `127.0.0.1:5000/`. An unknown transport, and
1216	  credentials given for an `oci` or `dir` side, are refused the same way. The
1217	  `oci` and `dir` locations are paths and are not read as hosts.
1218	- *Credentials.* A side with no credentials gets `--src-no-creds` /
1219	  `--dest-no-creds` / `--no-creds`; a side with credentials gets `--*authfile
1220	  <file>`, a container auth file `{"auths":{"<host[:port]>":{"auth":"<base64
1221	  user:password>"}}}`. There is one file per side, so the credentials of one are
1222	  never offered to the other. No password is ever an argument (visible through
1223	  `/proc`) or an environment variable. `Credentials` implements `fmt.Formatter`
1224	  (every verb, `%d` and `%x` included, prints `Credentials{User: <redacted>,
1225	  Password: REDACTED`), `String`, `GoString` and `slog.LogValuer`, and the
1226	  password has `json:"-"`.
1227	- *Working folder.* Each call makes `os.MkdirTemp` (`0700`), writes in it
1228	  `policy.json` (`{"default":[{"type":"insecureAcceptAnything"}]}`, given with
1229	  `--policy` before the subcommand; `--insecure-policy` is never used), an empty
1230	  `registries.conf` and the authentication files (`0600`), and `defer`s
1231	  `os.RemoveAll`. The folder is gone after a success, a skopeo failure and a
1232	  cancellation (the tests point `TMPDIR` at a folder and require it empty).
1233	- *Environment* (`skopeoEnvironment(registriesConf)`, modelled on
1234	  `gitEnvironment`): the caller's, without `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,
1235	  `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` (any case), `REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE` and every `CONTAINERS_*`
1236	  variable, then `CONTAINERS_REGISTRIES_CONF=<the empty file>`, so no proxy,
1237	  mirror, login or policy of the host applies. Names are compared in upper case
1238	  (Windows). `HOME` and `PATH` are kept.
1239	- *Digest.* `ManifestDigest` runs `skopeo inspect --raw` (stdout capped at 4 MiB)
1240	  and computes the sha256 in Go, so the answer does not depend on anything skopeo
1241	  says about the manifest. `Copy` takes `--preserve-digests` from the options.
1242	- *Errors.* Always a `*BenchError`. The stderr of skopeo (capped at 64 KiB) only
1243	  picks the kind through `classifySkopeo` and is never in a message, nor is its
1244	  stdout; `Err` is the exit status of the process. A cancelled or expired context
1245	  is `Unclassified` or `Deadline`. `classifySkopeo` matches lower-cased fragments:
1246	  `connection refused`, `no such host`, `i/o timeout` give `RegistryUnreachable`;
1247	  `unauthorized`, `denied:` and `requested access to the resource is denied`
1248	  (a bare `permission denied` of a local folder is `Unclassified`),
1249	  `authentication required` (what skopeo 1.18.0 says to
1250	  a push without a login, found by the real-skopeo test) and a whole-word `403`
1251	  (a port like 40399 does not count) give `RegistryRefused`; `manifest unknown`
1252	  gives `SeedFailed`; anything else `Unclassified`.
1253	
1254	**Accepted risks of the two doors** (audit of DEVDESK-539, single-user development
1255	machine):
1256	
1257	- The loopback guard checks the host of the registry reference only. It does not
1258	  check the `realm` of a Bearer challenge a registry sends back, so a registry
1259	  could point skopeo at another host to fetch a token; the registries the bench
1260	  talks to are the bench's own (the upstream through the port-forward, the bench
1261	  Nexus), which do not do it.
1262	- A SIGKILL of the Go process skips the `defer`s and the context kill: a
1263	  `kubectl port-forward` can outlive it, and the temporary folder
1264	  (`/tmp/devdesk-skopeo-*`, `0700`, with an authentication file `0600` holding the
1265	  admin password while a call ran) can stay on disk. Nothing sweeps them; remove
1266	  them by hand.
1267	- While a port-forward lives, its `127.0.0.1:<port>` is reachable by every local
1268	  account, without credentials of the upstream (which is anonymous by design).
1269	- `policy.json` is `insecureAcceptAnything`: no signature is checked. It is
1270	  bounded by the loopback guard (only the bench's own registries are reached),
1271	  not by the policy.
1272	
1273	**Tests.** The two doors are tested with the "helper process" pattern
1274	(`helper_process_test.go`): a one-line shell shim named `kubectl` or `skopeo` is the
1275	only thing on PATH and re-runs the test binary, which records its arguments,
1276	environment and the files it was pointed at (authentication file, policy,
1277	`registries.conf`, read while they exist), answers as the test asked and exits or
1278	hangs. `TestSkopeoAgainstFakeRegistry` runs the real skopeo against
1279	`fakeregistry_test.go`, an in-process OCI registry on the loopback with an
1280	optional Basic challenge (skipped without skopeo): HTTP fallback, credentials from
1281	the authentication file, `--preserve-digests` byte for byte, and the error kinds.
1282	None of it needs the cluster or `requireBench`; the source guards (below) list why
1283	each such test is exempt.
1284	
1285	## The upstream lifecycle (`upstream.go`, DEVDESK-540)
1286	
1287	`UpstreamState` is `UpstreamMissing` < `UpstreamCut` < `UpstreamStarting` <
1288	`UpstreamReady`. Neither function runs a preflight: the callers do (`Deploy`,
1289	then the seed, `RunPreflight(OpSeed)`).
1290	
1291	`ReadUpstream(ctx, runner, p)` reads only: `get deployment bench-upstream -n <ns>
1292	-o json` (the object by name, never the list), then, when one replica is wanted,
1293	`get pods -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=bench-upstream -o json`. A Deployment
1294	that is not there (`NotFound`) is Missing; zero replicas is Cut, even while an old
1295	pod is still terminating; otherwise a pod that is not terminating and whose `Ready`
1296	condition is `True` is Ready, else Starting (a pod that fails to pull is Starting,
1297	not an error: diagnosing is the wait's job). A failed read is a `*BenchError`
1298	classified like every other call.
1299	
1300	`EnsureUpstream(ctx, runner, clock, p, out)` reads first and writes at most once:
1301	
1302	| State read | Does |
1303	|---|---|
1304	| Missing | an error naming `bench-upstream` and `mise run nexus-bench:up` (`Deploy` applies the Deployment); no write |
1305	| Ready | nothing: no write, no wait |
1306	| Starting | no write; the wait |
1307	| Cut | `kubectl scale deployment/bench-upstream --replicas=1 -n <ns>` once (a failed scale is classified and not retried), then the wait |
1308	
1309	A custom upstream (`!p.UpstreamIsBench()`) is refused before any call, with an
1310	error that names `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL`: the bench scales the upstream it
1311	deploys and nothing else. The wait is the one of `Deploy` without the hosts: a
1312	round (`round()`, shared) reads the pods of the upstream and the claim
1313	`bench-upstream-data`, diagnoses them with `upstreamWorkload()`, then ends on a
1314	ready pod, on the deadline (`Params.Timeout`, within one interval; a `Deadline`
1315	that cites the pod and names `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`, or the pending reading that
1316	was still there) or sleeps `upstreamPollInterval` (2 s: a registry starts in
1317	seconds, and nothing is probed). A cancelled context is returned as is.
1318	`CutUpstream`, the recycling of the storage and the `OpCut`, `OpRestore` and
1319	`OpReset` preflights come with NX-02b.
1320	
1321	**Rights.** `up` gained, after its fourteen, patch `deployments/scale`, create
1322	`pods/portforward` and get `services` (namespace); `seed` asks get `deployments`,
1323	list `pods`, get `pods`, get `services`, create `pods/portforward` and patch
1324	`deployments/scale`. `kubectl port-forward svc/bench-upstream` fetches the Service,
1325	lists the pods of its selector, gets the pod it picks, then posts to
1326	`pods/portforward`: that is why `get services` and `get pods` are asked, on top of
1327	`list pods`.
1328	
1329	## The seed (`seed.go`, DEVDESK-542, NX-02a)
1330	
1331	`Seed(ctx, SeedDeps{Runner, Forwarder, Copier, Clock, Store}, baseURL, p, out)`
1332	puts the data set (D-I, `Dataset()`) in place and returns it as a `SeedResult`
1333	(digests filled, `PullThrough` true exactly for the images cached by
1334	`docker-proxy`). It never scales, applies or writes to Nexus (every request it
1335	sends is a `GET` as `admin`), and it runs no preflight: the caller does.
1336	
1337	**Order.**
1338	
1339	1. The stored credentials (`adminFromStore`, then the `bench-pull` password): a
1340	   missing one is `ProvisionFailed` that says to run `mise run nexus-bench:up`,
1341	   before any kubectl call or request.
1342	2. The upstream: a custom `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` is `SeedFailed` (the proxy

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

1	// Command nexus-bench deploys, provisions, inspects and destroys the disposable
2	// Nexus Community bench of DEVDESK-504 on a k0s cluster. It is a development
3	// tool driven by the mise tasks nexus-bench:*, outside mise run ci; see
4	// docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md.
5	package main
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"flag"
11		"fmt"
12		"io"
13		"os"
14		"os/signal"
15		"syscall"
16	
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/nexusbench"
18	)
19	
20	// Exit codes.
21	const (
22		exitOK      = 0
23		exitFailure = 1
24		exitUsage   = 2
25	)
26	
27	// deps is everything the command needs that reaches a cluster or the network,
28	// so that the tests run it with fakes. The zero value is enough for render,
29	// which uses none of it.
30	type deps struct {
31		newRunner  func(kubeContext string) (nexusbench.Runner, error)
32		newProber  func() nexusbench.Prober
33		clock      nexusbench.Clock
34		newStore   func(path string) (nexusbench.SecretStore, error)
35		newInitial func(r nexusbench.Runner, namespace string) nexusbench.InitialPassword
36		preflight  func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, p nexusbench.Params, op nexusbench.Op) (nexusbench.PreflightResult, error)
37		deploy     func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, pr nexusbench.Prober, clk nexusbench.Clock, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.DeployResult, error)
38		provision  func(ctx context.Context, baseURL string, ip nexusbench.InitialPassword, store nexusbench.SecretStore, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.ProvisionResult, error)
39		destroy    func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, clk nexusbench.Clock, store nexusbench.SecretStore, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) error
40	
41		// NX-02a (DEVDESK-544): the doors of the seed and the reads of status.
42		newForwarder   func(kubeContext string) (nexusbench.PortForwarder, error)
43		newCopier      func() (nexusbench.ImageCopier, error)
44		ensureUpstream func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, clk nexusbench.Clock, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) error
45		seed           func(ctx context.Context, d nexusbench.SeedDeps, baseURL string, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.SeedResult, error)
46		readUpstream   func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, p nexusbench.Params) (nexusbench.UpstreamState, error)
47		readImages     func(ctx context.Context, baseURL, repository string) ([]listedImage, error)
48	}

50	// defaultDeps wires the real kubectl, HTTP client, clock and files.
51	func defaultDeps() deps {
52		return deps{
53			newRunner:  nexusbench.NewExecRunner,
54			newProber:  nexusbench.NewProber,
55			clock:      nexusbench.NewClock(),
56			newStore:   nexusbench.NewFileStore,
57			newInitial: nexusbench.NewKubectlInitialPassword,
58			preflight:  nexusbench.RunPreflight,
59			deploy:     nexusbench.Deploy,
60			provision:  nexusbench.Provision,
61			destroy:    nexusbench.Destroy,
62	
63			newForwarder:   nexusbench.NewExecPortForwarder,
64			newCopier:      nexusbench.NewSkopeoCopier,
65			ensureUpstream: nexusbench.EnsureUpstream,

69		}

72	func main() {
73		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
74		// After the first signal cancels ctx, hand the signals back to the default
75		// behavior so that a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down.
76		context.AfterFunc(ctx, stop)
77		code := run(ctx, os.Args[1:], os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())
78		stop()
79		os.Exit(code)
80	}
81	
82	// session is one subcommand being run: its context, its resolved parameters and
83	// its streams.
84	type session struct {
85		ctx    context.Context
86		p      nexusbench.Params
87		getenv func(string) string
88		stdout io.Writer
89		stderr io.Writer
90		d      deps
91		// restHost is where the REST API is reached; explicit tells whether the
92		// operator chose it.
93		restHost string
94		explicit bool
95	}
96	
97	// run executes one command line and returns the exit code: 0 for success, 1
98	// for a failure of the bench, 2 for a mistake in the command line.
99	func run(ctx context.Context, args []string, getenv func(string) string, stdout, stderr io.Writer, d deps) int {
100		if len(args) == 0 {
101			printUsage(stderr)
102			return exitUsage
103		}
104		name := args[0]
105		switch name {
106		case "-h", "--help", "help":
107			printUsage(stdout)
108			return exitOK
109		case "up", "provision", "down", "seed", "status", "render":
110		default:
111			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus-bench: unknown subcommand %q\n\n", name)
112			printUsage(stderr)
113			return exitUsage
114		}
115	
116		flags := newFlagSet(name)
117		if err := flags.parse(args[1:]); err != nil {
118			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
119				printSubcommandHelp(stdout, name, flags)
120				return exitOK
121			}
122			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus-bench %s: %v\nRun nexus-bench %s -h for the flags.\n", name, err, name)
123			return exitUsage
124		}
125	
126		s := &session{ctx: ctx, getenv: getenv, stdout: stdout, stderr: stderr, d: d, restHost: loopbackHost}
127		p, err := flags.resolveParams(getenv)
128		if err != nil {
129			return s.fail(err)
130		}
131		s.p = p
132		if host, given := flags.restHostGiven(); given {
133			if err := validateRESTHost(host); err != nil {
134				return s.fail(err)
135			}
136			if name == "seed" && !isLoopbackHost(host) {
137				return s.fail(errors.New("seed always reaches Nexus and copies the images through 127.0.0.1, so --rest-host must be a loopback address"))
138			}
139			s.restHost, s.explicit = host, true
140		}
141	
142		switch name {
143		case "up":
144			return s.up()
145		case "provision":
146			return s.provision()
147		case "down":
148			return s.down()
149		case "seed":
150			return s.seed()
151		case "status":
152			return s.status()
153		default:
154			return s.render()
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// fail prints err on stderr and returns the failure code. A BenchError (also
159	// when wrapped or joined) is printed as its own message and nothing else: the
160	// text around it and the error it wraps can carry what a sub-process printed,
161	// a credential included. A cancelled run says so.
162	func (s *session) fail(err error) int {
163		var be *nexusbench.BenchError
164		switch {
165		case errors.As(err, &be):
166			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, be.Error())
167		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
168			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, "cancelled; the cluster keeps what was already done, run nexus-bench status to see it")
169		default:
170			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, err.Error())
171		}
172		return exitFailure
173	}
174	
175	// warn prints a warning on stderr.
176	func (s *session) warn(format string, args ...any) {
177		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(s.stderr, "warning: "+format+"\n", args...)
178	}
179	
180	// restURL is the REST origin the credentials are sent to.
181	func (s *session) restURL() string {
182		return nexusbench.RESTBaseURL(s.restHost, s.p)
183	}
184	
185	// warnIfClearText says so when the admin credentials leave this machine.
186	func (s *session) warnIfClearText() {
187		if s.explicit && !isLoopbackHost(s.restHost) {
188			s.warn("%s is plain HTTP: the credentials travel in clear text to %s", s.restURL(), s.restHost)
189		}
190	}

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

3	// tool driven by the mise tasks nexus-bench:*, outside mise run ci; see
4	// docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md.

6

8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"flag"
11		"fmt"
12		"io"
13		"os"
14		"os/signal"

17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/nexusbench"
18	)
19	
20	// Exit codes.
21	const (
22		exitOK      = 0
23		exitFailure = 1
24		exitUsage   = 2
25	)
26	
27	// deps is everything the command needs that reaches a cluster or the network,
28	// so that the tests run it with fakes. The zero value is enough for render,
29	// which uses none of it.
30	type deps struct {
31		newRunner  func(kubeContext string) (nexusbench.Runner, error)
32		newProber  func() nexusbench.Prober
33		clock      nexusbench.Clock
34		newStore   func(path string) (nexusbench.SecretStore, error)

36		preflight  func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, p nexusbench.Params, op nexusbench.Op) (nexusbench.PreflightResult, error)
37		deploy     func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, pr nexusbench.Prober, clk nexusbench.Clock, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.DeployResult, error)
38		provision  func(ctx context.Context, baseURL string, ip nexusbench.InitialPassword, store nexusbench.SecretStore, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.ProvisionResult, error)

42		newForwarder   func(kubeContext string) (nexusbench.PortForwarder, error)

44		ensureUpstream func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, clk nexusbench.Clock, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) error
45		seed           func(ctx context.Context, d nexusbench.SeedDeps, baseURL string, p nexusbench.Params, out io.Writer) (nexusbench.SeedResult, error)
46		readUpstream   func(ctx context.Context, r nexusbench.Runner, p nexusbench.Params) (nexusbench.UpstreamState, error)
47		readImages     func(ctx context.Context, baseURL, repository string) ([]listedImage, error)
48	}

51	func defaultDeps() deps {
52		return deps{
53			newRunner:  nexusbench.NewExecRunner,
54			newProber:  nexusbench.NewProber,
55			clock:      nexusbench.NewClock(),
56			newStore:   nexusbench.NewFileStore,
57			newInitial: nexusbench.NewKubectlInitialPassword,
58			preflight:  nexusbench.RunPreflight,
59			deploy:     nexusbench.Deploy,

72	func main() {
73		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
74		// After the first signal cancels ctx, hand the signals back to the default
75		// behavior so that a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down.
76		context.AfterFunc(ctx, stop)
77		code := run(ctx, os.Args[1:], os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())
78		stop()
79		os.Exit(code)
80	}
81	
82	// session is one subcommand being run: its context, its resolved parameters and
83	// its streams.
84	type session struct {
85		ctx    context.Context
86		p      nexusbench.Params
87		getenv func(string) string
88		stdout io.Writer
89		stderr io.Writer
90		d      deps
91		// restHost is where the REST API is reached; explicit tells whether the
92		// operator chose it.
93		restHost string
94		explicit bool
95	}
96	
97	// run executes one command line and returns the exit code: 0 for success, 1
98	// for a failure of the bench, 2 for a mistake in the command line.
99	func run(ctx context.Context, args []string, getenv func(string) string, stdout, stderr io.Writer, d deps) int {
100		if len(args) == 0 {
101			printUsage(stderr)
102			return exitUsage
103		}
104		name := args[0]
105		switch name {
106		case "-h", "--help", "help":
107			printUsage(stdout)
108			return exitOK
109		case "up", "provision", "down", "seed", "status", "render":
110		default:
111			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus-bench: unknown subcommand %q\n\n", name)
112			printUsage(stderr)
113			return exitUsage
114		}
115	
116		flags := newFlagSet(name)
117		if err := flags.parse(args[1:]); err != nil {
118			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
119				printSubcommandHelp(stdout, name, flags)
120				return exitOK
121			}
122			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "nexus-bench %s: %v\nRun nexus-bench %s -h for the flags.\n", name, err, name)
123			return exitUsage
124		}
125	
126		s := &session{ctx: ctx, getenv: getenv, stdout: stdout, stderr: stderr, d: d, restHost: loopbackHost}
127		p, err := flags.resolveParams(getenv)
128		if err != nil {
129			return s.fail(err)
130		}
131		s.p = p
132		if host, given := flags.restHostGiven(); given {
133			if err := validateRESTHost(host); err != nil {
134				return s.fail(err)
135			}
136			if name == "seed" && !isLoopbackHost(host) {
137				return s.fail(errors.New("seed always reaches Nexus and copies the images through 127.0.0.1, so --rest-host must be a loopback address"))
138			}
139			s.restHost, s.explicit = host, true
140		}
141	
142		switch name {
143		case "up":
144			return s.up()
145		case "provision":
146			return s.provision()
147		case "down":
148			return s.down()
149		case "seed":
150			return s.seed()
151		case "status":
152			return s.status()
153		default:
154			return s.render()
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// fail prints err on stderr and returns the failure code. A BenchError (also
159	// when wrapped or joined) is printed as its own message and nothing else: the
160	// text around it and the error it wraps can carry what a sub-process printed,
161	// a credential included. A cancelled run says so.
162	func (s *session) fail(err error) int {
163		var be *nexusbench.BenchError
164		switch {
165		case errors.As(err, &be):
166			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, be.Error())
167		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
168			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, "cancelled; the cluster keeps what was already done, run nexus-bench status to see it")
169		default:
170			_, _ = fmt.Fprintln(s.stderr, err.Error())
171		}
172		return exitFailure
173	}
174	
175	// warn prints a warning on stderr.
176	func (s *session) warn(format string, args ...any) {
177		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(s.stderr, "warning: "+format+"\n", args...)
178	}
179	
180	// restURL is the REST origin the credentials are sent to.
181	func (s *session) restURL() string {
182		return nexusbench.RESTBaseURL(s.restHost, s.p)
183	}
184	
185	// warnIfClearText says so when the admin credentials leave this machine.
186	func (s *session) warnIfClearText() {
187		if s.explicit && !isLoopbackHost(s.restHost) {
188			s.warn("%s is plain HTTP: the credentials travel in clear text to %s", s.restURL(), s.restHost)
189		}
190	}

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,

| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an

# The nexus-bench:* tasks (DEVDESK-504, docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md) drive a
# disposable Nexus on a real k0s cluster through kubectl: up, provision, down,
# seed and status read or change that cluster, and the bench has to be reachable from this
# machine. They are NOT part of ci, check, test or test-race and nothing depends
# on them (mise_tasks_test.go checks it). Only render contacts nothing.
#
# kubectl is declared on each task that reaches the cluster rather than in
# [tools], so the CI does not install it; render contacts nothing and has none.
# seed (DEVDESK-505) also needs skopeo, which is a tool of the host: mise does
# not install it and the description of the task says so.
# The cluster (datomir) runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is supported within one
# minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest accepted here.
# Arguments go after `--`: mise appends them to the command, so
# `mise run nexus-bench:up -- --namespace nexus-bench-2` reaches the command.
# Every flag has a NEXUS_BENCH_* variable; see `nexus-bench <subcommand> -h`.

[tasks."nexus-bench:up"]
description = "Deploy the disposable Nexus bench and its upstream on the cluster, wait for it, provision it, seed the data set and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster; --accept-eula needed once; seeding needs skopeo on this machine)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up"

[tasks."nexus-bench:provision"]
description = "Provision the running Nexus bench again (idempotent) and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench provision"

[tasks."nexus-bench:down"]
description = "Delete the Nexus bench namespace and wait until it is gone (acts on the cluster)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench down"

[tasks."nexus-bench:seed"]
description = "Put the data set in the Nexus bench that up provisioned and write the descriptor (acts on the cluster; needs skopeo on this machine, which mise does not install)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench seed"

[tasks."nexus-bench:status"]
description = "Report on the Nexus bench: pod, REST answer, upstream, descriptor drift, data set (reads the cluster, changes nothing)"
tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench status"

[tasks."nexus-bench:render"]
description = "Print the Nexus bench manifests for the current parameters (contacts nothing)"
run = "go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench render"

tools = { kubectl = "1.35" }

The search didn't find a documented REST call that clears an auto-block, but it did cover the related behavior.

- **How auto-blocking works:** Nexus marks a proxy's remote as unavailable after timeouts or repeated remote failures, and it will auto unblock the repo once it becomes reachable again. A remote that doesn't respond within the read timeout is auto-blocked, and Nexus Repository will check the health of the remote periodically.
- **Cache invalidation:** The REST call is a POST to /service/rest/v1/repositories/npm-group/invalidate-cache (the example uses a group repo). An older API doc describes the same action as expiring the cache of items in a proxy repository so the remote will be rechecked on next access. That makes it a way to force a recheck, but the sources don't say it clears the auto-block flag.
- **Persistent auto-block:** If the root path of the remote is unreachable but subdirectories work, you will need to disable the auto-block feature in your proxy repository's configuration. Users have also reported a proxy that stayed in auto-blocked status even after the upstream recovered (community.sonatype.com thread 8354).
- **Manual blocking via API:** One community user reported that changing the blocked flag through scripting was not retained after a restart. Another said that single fields couldn't be changed through the REST API without redefining the whole repository. Both reports are anecdotal.

Gap: I found no official endpoint to manually clear an auto-block. Verify against the Swagger doc at /service/rest/swagger.json on your instance, or check the Sonatype support article on auto-blocked status.

101:**D158 — DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a): the bench seeds a registry upstream inside its namespace, fed by a dataset generated in Go and pushed by skopeo, and cuts it by scaling to zero. Decided (user, archived 2026-11-17; plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, drafted there under this number; Q1 to Q4 settled as recommended, except where stated): (1) The client is the host's `skopeo` (1.18.0 when planned; not pinned by mise), run as a process by `skopeo.go` with a cleaned environment and an explicit policy; a missing binary is `SkopeoMissing`. The bench does not measure Nexus with the client that populated it. (2) The images are generated in Go at seed time as OCI layouts in a temporary directory: uncompressed layer tar, sorted entries, zero timestamps, no `created` in the config, so the digests are stable and pinned in a golden file. A `layerGzip` constant switches the layer to gzip, without name or date, if Nexus refuses uncompressed layers (H-LAYER). Nothing is committed as a binary and nothing comes from the network. (3) The upstream is a `registry:3.0.0` Deployment `bench-upstream` in the namespace, with PVC `bench-upstream-data` (kept across a cut, deleted only by `reset`) and a ClusterIP Service `bench-upstream:5000`. The Deployment manifest carries no `replicas`, so `kubectl scale` owns that field and server-side apply never fights it: a cut scales to 0, a restore to 1. The development machine reaches the upstream by `kubectl port-forward` on loopback, for the seed only. No NodePort: a writable registry is not exposed to the LAN. The PVC is read by name, not by label (this corrects a latent NX-01 bug). (4) The hosted repository is seeded through path routing on the HTTP port (`127.0.0.1:<HTTPNodePort>/docker-hosted/...`). Path routing is off by default on Nexus 3.98.1 (`docker.pathEnabled` is null and `/v2/` answers 404 on the HTTP port): `Provision` sets `pathEnabled: true` on `docker-hosted` and `docker-proxy` (lifted on the real bench, 2026-11-17). (5) TLS verification is disabled only for references whose host is `127.0.0.1` or `::1`, and only with a mandatory path. `seed` refuses a `--rest-host` that is not loopback. Credentials go through a temporary authfile (`0600` in a `0700` directory), never in argv. (6) The dataset is fixed in `dataset.go` and described in the descriptor: `api:1.0.0` and `api:1.1.0`, `team/api:1.0.0` and `tools/cli:0.1.0` in hosted; `shared/base:1.0` in hosted and in the upstream, with different content and digests; `mirror/cached:1.0` in the upstream, pulled once through the proxy; `mirror/uncached:1.0` in the upstream, never pulled. Each image carries a `org.devdesk.nexus-bench.source` label. (7) Absence is proven by a sentinel, `errImageAbsent`, returned only on a registry "manifest unknown"; any other failure stays an error, so an unreachable registry is never read as an empty one. (8) An unlisted digest is accepted. (9) Preflight checks the subresources the code uses (`kubectl auth can-i --subresource`: `deployments/scale`, `pods/portforward`), correcting an NX-01 defect that checked `pods/exec`. (10) `up` is extended: deploy Nexus and the upstream, bring the upstream to one ready replica, provision (the proxy is created and joins the group), seed, then write the descriptor, and only after full success. `seed` alone seeds. (11) The descriptor moves to schema 2 (`registryAccess`, `upstream`, `dataset`); `LoadDescriptor` rejects version 1. Rejected: a native Go registry client (it would share the bias of the client being measured); a public image from Docker Hub (network, mutable tags); an unauthenticated NodePort for the upstream (a writable registry on the LAN); `emptyDir` with reseeding (ad hoc content lost at each cut). (13) Nexus 3.98 enables an SSRF protection on a new installation and refuses a proxy whose remote URL host resolves to a private address, a ClusterIP included (HTTP 400 on `proxy.remoteUrl`). Decided on the real bench (2026-11-17): `Provision` adds the host of the bench upstream to `allowedDomains` of `/v1/security/ssrf-protection` before it creates the proxy, keeps the entries already there, never switches the protection on or off, and does nothing for an upstream URL the bench did not deploy (that refusal is explained with the endpoint to edit). Narrower than turning the protection off. (12) The story is split: NX-02a is DEVDESK-505 (upstream, proxy created, seed, descriptor; CA1, CA2, CA3, CA5, CA6); NX-02b is DEVDESK-534 (cut and restore, reset, proxy unblock, repository deletion; CA4, CA7). Why: one client and one dataset for every later measure, without a cluster-wide exposure, and a cut that the proxy cannot mistake for an empty registry. No separate ADR: the decision is local to the bench and reversible. **Reserves:** lifted on the real bench on 2026-11-17 (see "Observed on the real bench (NX-02a)" in `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`): H-PATH (false by default, fixed by `pathEnabled`), H-PUSH, H-LAYER, H-PROXYHTTP, H-DNS, H-UPRUN, H-SCALE and H-COMPONENTS held; H-SSRF was a surprise (13). H-UNBLOCK, H-STALE, H-CUTDELAY and H-REPODEL belong to NX-02b and are still assumptions. The duplicate `shared/base:1.0` has two digests. `descriptor.json` is versioned at schema 2. **Plane:** DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a), DEVDESK-534 (NX-02b). Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, `internal/nexusbench/`, `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md` (NX-02); D157.**
